- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#5 ("Confirm the paper's Method account against your code") by `experiment-repo`  > C7 and leakage results are in (`results/semisynth.parquet`, `results/matrix_facts.parquet`, code `experiments/run_c7.py`, `fit_semisynth.py`; delivered with the next code push). What the code computes, for the Method:
  > 
  > - Generator: logit P = mu + a_i + b_k + U_i.V_k, rank/penalty chosen by held-out log-likelihood on 10% masked cells (grid rank {1,3,5,8,12,20} x l2 {0.001,0.005,0.02}). Selected rank 20, l2 0.005, held-out ll -0.1207. The rank is at the upper edge of the grid but the curve is flat (rank 12: -0.1232), so say "selected from a grid; the likelihood is flat beyond rank ~12".
  > - Checks 1-3 (3 random half splits of the 1500 items; generator fitted on half A, prediction for half-B pool size, truth = accuracy on half-B items outside S; measured interval = item-bootstrap percentile, centred on the point estimate, Monte-Carlo noise included so it is conservative): predicted gap inside the measured interval in 24/24 (check 1, split-half), 23/24 (check 2, fitted on 75 of 128 configs predicting 128), 24/24 fitted, 24/24 independent-configuration and 23/24 equicorrelated dependence (check 3). Mean predicted-minus-measured gap +0.0035 (check 1; measured gap about 0.062), +0.0009 (check 2), so the generator slightly overstates the gap (about 6%). The interval is wide (about 0.039), so "inside" is a weak test and the three dependence modes are NOT distinguished by it; do not claim the check discriminates the dependence model.
  > - Curves: fitted on all items, n up to 800 and K up to 512 (validated support: n <= 200, K <= 128; the rest is extrapolation, mark it so). Max-t lower bound coverage 0.96-0.99, Bonferroni 0.99-1.00 (conservative) across the grid.
  > - Leakage probe (Tab 1): delta_leak = 0.42, 95% CI 0.22-0.62, computed on only 9 probe items (the CI is an item bootstrap over those 9); describe it as a small probe, not a rate for the benchmark.
  > - Interval conventions changed since your last read: real-arm pool-bootstrap intervals are now the bootstrap spread placed on the point estimate (resampled pools contain duplicated items, so their mean is not the pool's value), and a spread that cannot be separated from Monte-Carlo noise is returned as an unshrunk upper bound (flag `ci_mc_limited` / `se_between` NaN). Real C4 uses R=40 pool-bootstrap replicates, not 200 (the 200 x 200 account applies to the gap/C2 runs only).
